text: α2-Chimaerin, a Rac-specific GTPase-activating protein (RacGAP) isoform, refines dendritic spine morphology during late postnatal development, thereby determining adult spine features. Using mice with global and conditional knock-out of α-chimaerin isoforms, disrupting α2-chimaerin (but not α1-chimaerin) increased spine size and density in the hippocampus, whereas overexpressing α2-chimaerin in developing hippocampal neurons decreased spine size. α2-Chimaerin disruption suppressed EphA-mediated spine morphogenesis in cultured developing neurons. Juvenile-stage α2-chimaerin deletion increased adult hippocampal spine size and contextual fear learning; adult-only deletion left spine morphology and contextual learning unaltered. These results indicate developmental α2-chimaerin signaling determines adult spine morphology and normal cognitive ability.
